q: Which term matches this definition? “An organization that strives for a profit by providing goods and services desired by its customers.”
why: business: An organization that strives for a profit by providing goods and services desired by its customers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The inputs, such as tools, machinery, equipment, and buildings, used to produce goods and services and get them to the customer.”
why: capital: The inputs, such as tools, machinery, equipment, and buildings, used to produce goods and services and get them to the customer.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Expenses incurred from creating and selling goods and services.”
why: costs: Expenses incurred from creating and selling goods and services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “People who combine the inputs of natural resources, labor, and capital to produce goods or services with the intention of making a profit or accomplishing a not-for-profit goal.”
why: entrepreneurs: People who combine the inputs of natural resources, labor, and capital to produce goods or services with the intention of making a profit or accomplishing a not-for-profit goal.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The resources used to create goods and services.”
why: factors of production: The resources used to create goods and services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Tangible items manufactured by businesses.”
why: goods: Tangible items manufactured by businesses.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The study of people’s vital statistics, such as their age, gender, race and ethnicity, and location.”
why: demography: The study of people’s vital statistics, such as their age, gender, race and ethnicity, and location.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The amount of goods and services one worker can produce.”
why: productivity: The amount of goods and services one worker can produce.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The application of science and engineering skills and knowledge to solve production and organizational problems.”
why: technology: The application of science and engineering skills and knowledge to solve production and organizational problems.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An economic system based on competition in the marketplace and private ownership of the factors of production (resources); also known as the private enterprise system.”
why: capitalism: An economic system based on competition in the marketplace and private ownership of the factors of production (resources); also known as the private enterprise system.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The movement of inputs and outputs among households, businesses, and governments; a way of showing how the sectors of the economy interact.”
why: circular flow: The movement of inputs and outputs among households, businesses, and governments; a way of showing how the sectors of the economy interact.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An economic system characterized by government ownership of virtually all resources, government control of all markets, and economic decision-making by central government planning.”
why: communism: An economic system characterized by government ownership of virtually all resources, government control of all markets, and economic decision-making by central government planning.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The combination of policies, laws, and choices made by a nation’s government to establish the systems that determine what goods and services are produced and how they are allocated.”
why: economic system: The combination of policies, laws, and choices made by a nation’s government to establish the systems that determine what goods and services are produced and how they are allocated.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The study of how a society uses scarce resources to produce and distribute goods and services.”
why: economics: The study of how a society uses scarce resources to produce and distribute goods and services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The subarea of economics that focuses on the economy as a whole by looking at aggregate data for large groups of people, companies, or products.”
why: macroeconomics: The subarea of economics that focuses on the economy as a whole by looking at aggregate data for large groups of people, companies, or products.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Upward and downward changes in the level of economic activity.”
why: business cycles: Upward and downward changes in the level of economic activity.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An index of the prices of a “market basket” of goods and services purchased by typical urban consumers.”
why: consumer price index (CPI): An index of the prices of a “market basket” of goods and services purchased by typical urban consumers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Inflation that occurs when increases in production costs push up the prices of final goods and services.”
why: cost-push inflation: Inflation that occurs when increases in production costs push up the prices of final goods and services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Unemployment that occurs when a downturn in the business cycle reduces the demand for labor throughout the economy.”
why: cyclical unemployment: Unemployment that occurs when a downturn in the business cycle reduces the demand for labor throughout the economy.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Inflation that occurs when the demand for goods and services is greater than the supply.”
why: demand-pull inflation: Inflation that occurs when the demand for goods and services is greater than the supply.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An increase in a nation’s output of goods and services.”
why: economic growth: An increase in a nation’s output of goods and services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The use of monetary policy by the Federal Reserve System to tighten the money supply by selling government securities or raising interest rates.”
why: contractionary policy: The use of monetary policy by the Federal Reserve System to tighten the money supply by selling government securities or raising interest rates.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The situation that occurs when government spending replaces spending by the private sector.”
why: crowding out: The situation that occurs when government spending replaces spending by the private sector.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The use of monetary policy by the Fed to increase, or loosen, the growth of the money supply.”
why: expansionary policy: The use of monetary policy by the Fed to increase, or loosen, the growth of the money supply.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The condition that occurs when the federal government spends more for programs than it collects in taxes.”
why: federal budget deficit: The condition that occurs when the federal government spends more for programs than it collects in taxes.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The central banking system of the United States.”
why: Federal Reserve System (the Fed): The central banking system of the United States.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The government’s use of taxation and spending to affect the economy.”
why: fiscal policy: The government’s use of taxation and spending to affect the economy.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The quantity of a good or service that people are willing to buy at various prices.”
why: demand: The quantity of a good or service that people are willing to buy at various prices.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A graph showing the quantity of a good or service that people are willing to buy at various prices.”
why: demand curve: A graph showing the quantity of a good or service that people are willing to buy at various prices.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The point at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.”
why: equilibrium: The point at which quantity demanded equals quantity supplied.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The quantity of a good or service that businesses will make available at various prices.”
why: supply: The quantity of a good or service that businesses will make available at various prices.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A graph showing the quantity of a good or service that businesses will make available at various prices.”
why: supply curve: A graph showing the quantity of a good or service that businesses will make available at various prices.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Factors, such as technological or legal conditions, that prevent new firms from competing equally with an existing firm.”
why: barriers to entry: Factors, such as technological or legal conditions, that prevent new firms from competing equally with an existing firm.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The number of suppliers in a market.”
why: market structure: The number of suppliers in a market.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A market structure in which many firms offer products that are close substitutes and in which entry is relatively easy.”
why: monopolistic competition: A market structure in which many firms offer products that are close substitutes and in which entry is relatively easy.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A market structure in which a few firms produce most or all of the output and in which large capital requirements or other factors limit the number of firms.”
why: oligopoly: A market structure in which a few firms produce most or all of the output and in which large capital requirements or other factors limit the number of firms.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A market structure in which a large number of small firms sell similar products, buyers and sellers have good information, and businesses can be easily opened or closed.”
why: perfect (pure) competition: A market structure in which a large number of small firms sell similar products, buyers and sellers have good information, and businesses can be easily opened or closed.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A market structure in which a single firm accounts for all industry sales of a particular good or service and in which there are barriers to entry.”
why: pure monopoly: A market structure in which a single firm accounts for all industry sales of a particular good or service and in which there are barriers to entry.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The practice of building, maintaining, and enhancing interactions with customers and other parties to develop long-term satisfaction through mutually beneficial partnerships.”
why: relationship management: The practice of building, maintaining, and enhancing interactions with customers and other parties to develop long-term satisfaction through mutually beneficial partnerships.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A cooperative agreement between business firms; sometimes called a strategic partnership.”
why: strategic alliance: A cooperative agreement between business firms; sometimes called a strategic partnership.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A philosophy in which a person will follow his or her obligations to an individual or society because upholding one's duty is what is ethically correct.”
why: deontology: A philosophy in which a person will follow his or her obligations to an individual or society because upholding one's duty is what is ethically correct.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A situation where a person must choose from a set of actions that may be ethical or unethical.”
why: ethical issue: A situation where a person must choose from a set of actions that may be ethical or unethical.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A set of moral standards for judging whether something is right or wrong.”
why: ethics: A set of moral standards for judging whether something is right or wrong.

q: Which term matches this definition? “What is considered fair according to the prevailing standards of society; an equitable distribution of the burdens and rewards that society has to offer.”
why: justice: What is considered fair according to the prevailing standards of society; an equitable distribution of the burdens and rewards that society has to offer.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A philosophy that focuses on the consequences of an action to determine whether it is right or wrong; holds that an action that affects the majority adversely is morally wrong.”
why: utilitarianism: A philosophy that focuses on the consequences of an action to determine whether it is right or wrong; holds that an action that affects the majority adversely is morally wrong.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A set of guidelines prepared by a firm to provide its employees with the knowledge of what the firm expects in terms of their responsibilities and behavior toward fellow employees, customers, and suppliers.”
why: code of ethics: A set of guidelines prepared by a firm to provide its employees with the knowledge of what the firm expects in terms of their responsibilities and behavior toward fellow employees, customers, and suppliers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The concern of businesses for the welfare of society as a whole; consists of obligations beyond those required by law or contracts.”
why: corporate social responsibility (CSR): The concern of businesses for the welfare of society as a whole; consists of obligations beyond those required by law or contracts.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The practice of charitable giving by corporations; includes contributing cash, donating equipment and products, and supporting the volunteer efforts of company employees.”
why: corporate philanthropy: The practice of charitable giving by corporations; includes contributing cash, donating equipment and products, and supporting the volunteer efforts of company employees.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The practice of limiting investments to securities of companies that behave in accordance with the investor’s beliefs about ethical and social responsibility to encourage businesses to be more socially responsible.”
why: social investing: The practice of limiting investments to securities of companies that behave in accordance with the investor’s beliefs about ethical and social responsibility to encourage businesses to be more socially responsible.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Individuals or groups to whom a business has a responsibility; includes employees, customers, the general public, and investors.”
why: stakeholders: Individuals or groups to whom a business has a responsibility; includes employees, customers, the general public, and investors.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The practice of tying philanthropy and corporate social responsibility efforts closely to a company’s mission or goals and targeting donations to the communities where a company does business.”
why: strategic giving: The practice of tying philanthropy and corporate social responsibility efforts closely to a company’s mission or goals and targeting donations to the communities where a company does business.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A summary of a country’s international financial transactions showing the difference between the country’s total payments to and its total receipts from other countries.”
why: balance of payments: A summary of a country’s international financial transactions showing the difference between the country’s total payments to and its total receipts from other countries.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The difference between the value of a country’s exports and the value of its imports during a specific time.”
why: balance of trade: The difference between the value of a country’s exports and the value of its imports during a specific time.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A lowering of the value of a nation’s currency relative to other currencies.”
why: devaluation: A lowering of the value of a nation’s currency relative to other currencies.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Goods and services produced in one country and sold to other countries.”
why: exports: Goods and services produced in one country and sold to other countries.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A system in which prices of currencies move up and down based upon the demand for and supply of the various currencies.”
why: floating exchange rates: A system in which prices of currencies move up and down based upon the demand for and supply of the various currencies.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Goods and services that are bought from other countries.”
why: imports: Goods and services that are bought from other countries.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The situation when a country can produce and sell a product at a lower cost than any other country or when it is the only country that can provide the product.”
why: absolute advantage: The situation when a country can produce and sell a product at a lower cost than any other country or when it is the only country that can provide the product.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The policy of permitting the people and businesses of a country to buy and sell where they please without restrictions.”
why: free trade: The policy of permitting the people and businesses of a country to buy and sell where they please without restrictions.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Forum that brings together 19 countries plus the European Union and the African Union—the largest and fastest-growing economies in the world.”
why: G20: Forum that brings together 19 countries plus the European Union and the African Union—the largest and fastest-growing economies in the world.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Sending work functions to another country, resulting in domestic workers losing their jobs.”
why: outsourcing: Sending work functions to another country, resulting in domestic workers losing their jobs.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The concept that each country should specialize in the products that it can produce most readily and cheaply and trade those products for those that other countries can produce more readily and cheaply.”
why: principle of comparative advantage: The concept that each country should specialize in the products that it can produce most readily and cheaply and trade those products for those that other countries can produce more readily and cheaply.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The policy of protecting home industries from outside competition by establishing artificial barriers such as tariffs and quotas.”
why: protectionism: The policy of protecting home industries from outside competition by establishing artificial barriers such as tariffs and quotas.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Government rules that give special privileges to domestic manufacturers and retailers.”
why: buy-national regulations: Government rules that give special privileges to domestic manufacturers and retailers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A total ban on imports or exports of a product.”
why: embargo: A total ban on imports or exports of a product.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Laws that require a company earning foreign exchange (foreign currency) from its exports to sell the foreign exchange to a control agency, such as a central bank.”
why: exchange controls: Laws that require a company earning foreign exchange (foreign currency) from its exports to sell the foreign exchange to a control agency, such as a central bank.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A limit on the quantity of a certain good that can be imported.”
why: import quota: A limit on the quantity of a certain good that can be imported.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Tariffs that are imposed in order to make imports less attractive to buyers than domestic products are.”
why: protective tariffs: Tariffs that are imposed in order to make imports less attractive to buyers than domestic products are.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A tax imposed on imported goods.”
why: tariff: A tax imposed on imported goods.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The practice of charging a lower price for a product in foreign markets than in the firm’s home market.”
why: dumping: The practice of charging a lower price for a product in foreign markets than in the firm’s home market.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An international organization, founded in 1945, that promotes trade, makes short-term loans to member nations, and acts as a lender of last resort for troubled nations.”
why: International Monetary Fund (IMF): An international organization, founded in 1945, that promotes trade, makes short-term loans to member nations, and acts as a lender of last resort for troubled nations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A 1994 agreement originally signed by 117 nations to lower trade barriers worldwide.”
why: Uruguay Round: A 1994 agreement originally signed by 117 nations to lower trade barriers worldwide.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An international bank that offers low-interest loans, as well as advice and information, to developing nations.”
why: World Bank: An international bank that offers low-interest loans, as well as advice and information, to developing nations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An organization established by the Uruguay Round in 1994 to oversee international trade, reduce trade barriers, and resolve disputes among member nations.”
why: World Trade Organization (WTO): An organization established by the Uruguay Round in 1994 to oversee international trade, reduce trade barriers, and resolve disputes among member nations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The delegation of limited sovereignty by European Union member states to the EU so that common laws and policies can be created at the European level.”
why: European integration: The delegation of limited sovereignty by European Union member states to the EU so that common laws and policies can be created at the European level.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Trade agreement among 27 European nations.”
why: European Union: Trade agreement among 27 European nations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An area where the nations allow free, or almost free, trade among each other while imposing tariffs on goods of nations outside the zone.”
why: free-trade zone: An area where the nations allow free, or almost free, trade among each other while imposing tariffs on goods of nations outside the zone.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Trade agreement between Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.”
why: Mercosur: Trade agreement between Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A 1993 agreement creating a free-trade zone including Canada, Mexico, and the United States; now replaced by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).”
why: North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA): A 1993 agreement creating a free-trade zone including Canada, Mexico, and the United States; now replaced by the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).

q: Which term matches this definition? “A tariff that is lower for some nations than for others.”
why: preferential tariff: A tariff that is lower for some nations than for others.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The practice in which a foreign firm manufactures private-label goods under a domestic firm’s brand name.”
why: contract manufacturing: The practice in which a foreign firm manufactures private-label goods under a domestic firm’s brand name.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A form of international trade in which part or all of the payment for goods or services is in the form of other goods and services.”
why: countertrade: A form of international trade in which part or all of the payment for goods or services is in the form of other goods and services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Active ownership of a foreign company or of manufacturing or marketing facilities in a foreign country.”
why: direct foreign investment: Active ownership of a foreign company or of manufacturing or marketing facilities in a foreign country.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The practice of selling domestically produced goods to buyers in another country.”
why: exporting: The practice of selling domestically produced goods to buyers in another country.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An agreement in which a domestic firm buys part of a foreign firm or joins with a foreign firm to create a new entity.”
why: joint venture: An agreement in which a domestic firm buys part of a foreign firm or joins with a foreign firm to create a new entity.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The legal process whereby a firm agrees to allow another firm to use a manufacturing process, trademark, patent, trade secret, or other proprietary knowledge in exchange for the payment of a royalty.”
why: licensing: The legal process whereby a firm agrees to allow another firm to use a manufacturing process, trademark, patent, trade secret, or other proprietary knowledge in exchange for the payment of a royalty.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The basic institutions and public facilities upon which an economy’s development depends.”
why: infrastructure: The basic institutions and public facilities upon which an economy’s development depends.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A sense of national consciousness that boosts the culture and interests of one country over those of all other countries.”
why: nationalism: A sense of national consciousness that boosts the culture and interests of one country over those of all other countries.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Corporations that move resources, goods, services, and skills across national boundaries without regard to the country in which their headquarters are located.”
why: multinational corporations: Corporations that move resources, goods, services, and skills across national boundaries without regard to the country in which their headquarters are located.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A business that is established, owned, operated, and often financed by one person.”
why: sole proprietorship: A business that is established, owned, operated, and often financed by one person.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Partners who have unlimited liability for all of the firm’s business obligations and who control its operations.”
why: general partners: Partners who have unlimited liability for all of the firm’s business obligations and who control its operations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A partnership in which all partners share in the management and profits. Each partner can act on behalf of the firm and has unlimited liability for all its business obligations.”
why: general partnership: A partnership in which all partners share in the management and profits. Each partner can act on behalf of the firm and has unlimited liability for all its business obligations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Partners whose liability for the firm’s business obligations is limited to the amount of their investment. They help to finance the business but do not participate in the firm’s operations.”
why: limited partners: Partners whose liability for the firm’s business obligations is limited to the amount of their investment. They help to finance the business but do not participate in the firm’s operations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A partnership with one or more general partners, who have unlimited liability, and one or more limited partners, whose liability is limited to the amount of their investment in the company.”
why: limited partnership: A partnership with one or more general partners, who have unlimited liability, and one or more limited partners, whose liability is limited to the amount of their investment in the company.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An association of two or more individuals who agree to operate a business together for profit.”
why: partnership: An association of two or more individuals who agree to operate a business together for profit.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A group of people elected by the stockholders to handle the overall management of a corporation, such as setting major corporate goals and policies, hiring corporate officers, and overseeing the firm’s operations and finances.”
why: board of directors: A group of people elected by the stockholders to handle the overall management of a corporation, such as setting major corporate goals and policies, hiring corporate officers, and overseeing the firm’s operations and finances.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A conventional or basic form of corporate organization.”
why: C corporation: A conventional or basic form of corporate organization.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A hybrid organization that offers the same liability protection as a corporation but may be taxed as either a partnership or a corporation.”
why: limited liability company (LLC): A hybrid organization that offers the same liability protection as a corporation but may be taxed as either a partnership or a corporation.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A hybrid entity that is organized like a corporation, with stockholders, directors, and officers, but taxed like a partnership, with income and losses flowing through to the stockholders and taxed as their personal income.”
why: S corporation: A hybrid entity that is organized like a corporation, with stockholders, directors, and officers, but taxed like a partnership, with income and losses flowing through to the stockholders and taxed as their personal income.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The owners of a corporation who hold shares of stock that carry certain rights.”
why: stockholders (or shareholders): The owners of a corporation who hold shares of stock that carry certain rights.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A group of cooperative members who unite for combined purchasing power.”
why: buyer cooperative: A group of cooperative members who unite for combined purchasing power.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Two or more companies that form an alliance to pursue a specific project, usually for a specified time period.”
why: joint venture: Two or more companies that form an alliance to pursue a specific project, usually for a specified time period.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Individual producers who join together to compete more effectively with large producers.”
why: seller cooperative: Individual producers who join together to compete more effectively with large producers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “In a franchising arrangement, the individual or company that sells the goods or services of the franchisor in a certain geographic area.”
why: franchisee: In a franchising arrangement, the individual or company that sells the goods or services of the franchisor in a certain geographic area.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A form of business organization based on a business arrangement between a franchisor, which supplies the product or service concept, and the franchisee, who sells the goods or services of the franchisor in a certain geographic area.”
why: franchising: A form of business organization based on a business arrangement between a franchisor, which supplies the product or service concept, and the franchisee, who sells the goods or services of the franchisor in a certain geographic area.

q: Which term matches this definition? “In a franchising arrangement, the company that supplies the product or service concept to the franchisee.”
why: franchisor: In a franchising arrangement, the company that supplies the product or service concept to the franchisee.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The purchase of a target company by another corporation or by an investor group typically negotiated with the target company board of directors.”
why: acquisition: The purchase of a target company by another corporation or by an investor group typically negotiated with the target company board of directors.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A merger of companies in unrelated businesses; done to reduce risk.”
why: conglomerate merger: A merger of companies in unrelated businesses; done to reduce risk.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A merger of companies at the same stage in the same industry; done to reduce costs, expand product offerings, or reduce competition.”
why: horizontal merger: A merger of companies at the same stage in the same industry; done to reduce costs, expand product offerings, or reduce competition.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A corporate takeover financed by large amounts of borrowed money; can be started by outside investors or the corporation’s management.”
why: leveraged buyout (LBO): A corporate takeover financed by large amounts of borrowed money; can be started by outside investors or the corporation’s management.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The combination of two or more firms to form one new company.”
why: merger: The combination of two or more firms to form one new company.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A merger of companies at different stages in the same industry; done to gain control over supplies of resources or to gain access to different markets.”
why: vertical merger: A merger of companies at different stages in the same industry; done to gain control over supplies of resources or to gain access to different markets.

q: Which term matches this definition? “People with vision, drive, and creativity who are willing to take the risk of starting and managing a business to make a profit, or greatly changing the scope and direction of an existing firm.”
why: entrepreneurs: People with vision, drive, and creativity who are willing to take the risk of starting and managing a business to make a profit, or greatly changing the scope and direction of an existing firm.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Entrepreneurs who apply their creativity, vision, and risk-taking within a large corporation, rather than starting a company of their own.”
why: intrapreneurs: Entrepreneurs who apply their creativity, vision, and risk-taking within a large corporation, rather than starting a company of their own.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A business with under 500 employees that is independently managed, is owned by an individual or a small group of investors, is based locally, and is not a dominant company in its industry.”
why: small business: A business with under 500 employees that is independently managed, is owned by an individual or a small group of investors, is based locally, and is not a dominant company in its industry.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Individual investors or groups of experienced investors who provide financing for start-up businesses by investing their own funds.”
why: angel investors: Individual investors or groups of experienced investors who provide financing for start-up businesses by investing their own funds.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A form of business financing consisting of borrowed funds that must be repaid with interest over a stated time period.”
why: debt: A form of business financing consisting of borrowed funds that must be repaid with interest over a stated time period.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A form of business financing consisting of funds raised through the sale of stock (i.e., ownership) in a business.”
why: equity: A form of business financing consisting of funds raised through the sale of stock (i.e., ownership) in a business.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Financing obtained from venture capitalists, investment firms that specialize in financing small, high-growth companies and receive an ownership interest and a voice in management in return for their money.”
why: venture capital: Financing obtained from venture capitalists, investment firms that specialize in financing small, high-growth companies and receive an ownership interest and a voice in management in return for their money.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A government agency that advocates for small business; specifically it helps people start and manage small businesses, advises them in the areas of finance and management, and helps them win federal contracts.”
why: Small Business Administration (SBA): A government agency that advocates for small business; specifically it helps people start and manage small businesses, advises them in the areas of finance and management, and helps them win federal contracts.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Privately owned and managed investment companies that are licensed by the Small Business Administration and provide long-term financing for small businesses.”
why: Small Business Investment Company (SBIC): Privately owned and managed investment companies that are licensed by the Small Business Administration and provide long-term financing for small businesses.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The ability to produce the desired result or good.”
why: effectiveness: The ability to produce the desired result or good.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Using the least amount of resources to accomplish the organization’s goals.”
why: efficiency: Using the least amount of resources to accomplish the organization’s goals.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of guiding the development, maintenance, and allocation of resources to attain organizational goals.”
why: management: The process of guiding the development, maintenance, and allocation of resources to attain organizational goals.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Plans that identify alternative courses of action for very unusual or crisis situations; typically stipulate the chain of command, standard operating procedures, and communication channels the organization will use during an emergency.”
why: contingency plans: Plans that identify alternative courses of action for very unusual or crisis situations; typically stipulate the chain of command, standard operating procedures, and communication channels the organization will use during an emergency.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An organization’s purpose and reason for existing; its long-term goals.”
why: mission: An organization’s purpose and reason for existing; its long-term goals.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A statement that conveys an organization’s purpose and reason for existing and describes its basic philosophy.”
why: mission statement: A statement that conveys an organization’s purpose and reason for existing and describes its basic philosophy.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of creating specific standards, methods, policies, and procedures that are used in specific functional areas of the organization; helps guide and control the implementation of tactical plans.”
why: operational planning: The process of creating specific standards, methods, policies, and procedures that are used in specific functional areas of the organization; helps guide and control the implementation of tactical plans.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of deciding what needs to be done to achieve organizational objectives; identifying when and how it will be done; and determining who should do it.”
why: planning: The process of deciding what needs to be done to achieve organizational objectives; identifying when and how it will be done; and determining who should do it.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Managers who design and carry out operation plans for the ongoing daily activities of the firm.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “The highest level of managers; includes CEOs, presidents, and vice presidents, who develop strategic plans.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “Leaders who encourage discussion about issues and then require that all parties involved agree to the final decision.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “Leaders who confer with subordinates before making a decision but who retain the final decision-making authority.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “The set of attitudes, values, and standards that distinguishes one organization from another.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “Leaders who solicit input from all members of the group and then allow the members to make the final decision through a vote.”
why: democratic leaders: Leaders who solicit input from all members of the group and then allow the members to make the final decision through a vote.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of assessing the organization’s progress toward accomplishing its goals; includes monitoring the implementation of a plan and correcting deviations from the plan.”
why: controlling: The process of assessing the organization’s progress toward accomplishing its goals; includes monitoring the implementation of a plan and correcting deviations from the plan.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A manager’s activities as an entrepreneur, resource allocator, conflict resolver, or negotiator.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “A manager’s activities as an information gatherer, an information disseminator, or a spokesperson for the company.”
why: informational roles: A manager’s activities as an information gatherer, an information disseminator, or a spokesperson for the company.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A manager’s activities as a figurehead, company leader, or liaison.”
why: interpersonal roles: A manager’s activities as a figurehead, company leader, or liaison.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Responses to infrequent, unforeseen, or very unusual problems and opportunities where the manager does not have a precedent to follow in decision-making.”
why: nonprogrammed decisions: Responses to infrequent, unforeseen, or very unusual problems and opportunities where the manager does not have a precedent to follow in decision-making.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Decisions made in response to frequently occurring routine situations.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “A manager’s ability to view the organization as a whole, understand how the various parts are interdependent, and assess how the organization relates to its external environment.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “A manager’s interpersonal skills that are used to accomplish goals through the use of human resources.”

q: Which term matches this definition? “A manager’s specialized areas of knowledge and expertise, as well as the ability to apply that knowledge.”
why: technical skills: A manager’s specialized areas of knowledge and expertise, as well as the ability to apply that knowledge.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A manager’s ability to operate in diverse cultural environments.”
why: global management skills: A manager’s ability to operate in diverse cultural environments.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Departmentalization that is based on the primary type of customer served by the organizational unit.”
why: customer departmentalization: Departmentalization that is based on the primary type of customer served by the organizational unit.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of grouping jobs together so that similar or associated tasks and activities can be coordinated.”
why: departmentalization: The process of grouping jobs together so that similar or associated tasks and activities can be coordinated.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of dividing work into separate jobs and assigning tasks to workers.”
why: division of labor: The process of dividing work into separate jobs and assigning tasks to workers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Departmentalization that is based on the primary functions performed within an organizational unit.”
why: functional departmentalization: Departmentalization that is based on the primary functions performed within an organizational unit.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Departmentalization that is based on the geographic segmentation of the organizational units.”
why: geographic departmentalization: Departmentalization that is based on the geographic segmentation of the organizational units.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An organizational structure that includes both line and staff positions.”
why: line-and-staff organization: An organizational structure that includes both line and staff positions.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An organizational structure in which authority and responsibility are held by a group rather than an individual.”
why: committee structure: An organizational structure in which authority and responsibility are held by a group rather than an individual.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An organizational structure that combines functional and product departmentalization by bringing together people from different functional areas of the organization to work on a special project.”
why: matrix structure (project management): An organizational structure that combines functional and product departmentalization by bringing together people from different functional areas of the organization to work on a special project.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Members from the same organizational level but from different functional areas.”
why: cross-functional team: Members from the same organizational level but from different functional areas.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The degree to which group members want to stay in the group and tend to resist outside influences.”
why: group cohesiveness: The degree to which group members want to stay in the group and tend to resist outside influences.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Usually members of the same department who meet regularly to suggest ways to improve operations and solve specific problems.”
why: problem-solving teams: Usually members of the same department who meet regularly to suggest ways to improve operations and solve specific problems.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Teams without formal supervision that plan, select alternatives, and evaluate their own performance.”
why: self-managed work teams: Teams without formal supervision that plan, select alternatives, and evaluate their own performance.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The groups that share resources and coordinate efforts to help members better perform their individual jobs.”
why: work groups: The groups that share resources and coordinate efforts to help members better perform their individual jobs.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Like a work group but also requires the pooling of knowledge, skills, abilities, and resources to achieve a common goal.”
why: work teams: Like a work group but also requires the pooling of knowledge, skills, abilities, and resources to achieve a common goal.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Legitimate power, granted by the organization and acknowledged by employees, that allows an individual to request action and expect compliance.”
why: authority: Legitimate power, granted by the organization and acknowledged by employees, that allows an individual to request action and expect compliance.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The line of authority that extends from one level of an organization’s hierarchy to the next, from top to bottom, and makes clear who reports to whom.”
why: chain of command: The line of authority that extends from one level of an organization’s hierarchy to the next, from top to bottom, and makes clear who reports to whom.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The assignment of some degree of authority and responsibility to persons lower in the chain of command.”
why: delegation of authority: The assignment of some degree of authority and responsibility to persons lower in the chain of command.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The levels of management within an organization; typically includes top, middle, and supervisory management.”
why: managerial hierarchy: The levels of management within an organization; typically includes top, middle, and supervisory management.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The number of employees a manager directly supervises; also called span of management.”
why: span of control: The number of employees a manager directly supervises; also called span of management.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The degree to which formal authority is concentrated in one area or level of an organization. Top management makes most of the decisions.”
why: centralization: The degree to which formal authority is concentrated in one area or level of an organization. Top management makes most of the decisions.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of pushing decision-making authority down the organizational hierarchy.”
why: decentralization: The process of pushing decision-making authority down the organizational hierarchy.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An organizational structure that is characterized by a relatively high degree of job specialization, rigid departmentalization, many layers of management, narrow spans of control, centralized decision-making, and a long chain of command.”
why: mechanistic organization: An organizational structure that is characterized by a relatively high degree of job specialization, rigid departmentalization, many layers of management, narrow spans of control, centralized decision-making, and a long chain of command.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An organizational structure that is characterized by a relatively low degree of job specialization, loose departmentalization, few levels of management, wide spans of control, decentralized decision-making, and a short chain of command.”
why: organic organization: An organizational structure that is characterized by a relatively low degree of job specialization, loose departmentalization, few levels of management, wide spans of control, decentralized decision-making, and a short chain of command.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The order and design of relationships within a firm; consists of two or more people working together with a common objective and clarity of purpose.”
why: formal organization: The order and design of relationships within a firm; consists of two or more people working together with a common objective and clarity of purpose.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The network of connections and channels of communication based on the informal relationships of individuals inside an organization.”
why: informal organization: The network of connections and channels of communication based on the informal relationships of individuals inside an organization.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The complete redesign of business structures and processes in order to improve operations.”
why: reengineering: The complete redesign of business structures and processes in order to improve operations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A network of independent companies linked by information technology to share skills, costs, and access to one another’s markets; allows the companies to come together quickly to exploit rapidly changing opportunities.”
why: virtual corporation: A network of independent companies linked by information technology to share skills, costs, and access to one another’s markets; allows the companies to come together quickly to exploit rapidly changing opportunities.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Individual who has temporary employment, either full- or part-time, hired on a non-permanent basis.”
why: contingent worker: Individual who has temporary employment, either full- or part-time, hired on a non-permanent basis.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of hiring, developing, motivating, and evaluating employees to achieve organizational goals.”
why: human resource (HR) management: The process of hiring, developing, motivating, and evaluating employees to achieve organizational goals.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Creating a strategy for meeting current and future human resource needs.”
why: human resource planning: Creating a strategy for meeting current and future human resource needs.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A study of the tasks required to do a particular job well.”
why: job analysis: A study of the tasks required to do a particular job well.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The tasks and responsibilities of a job.”
why: job description: The tasks and responsibilities of a job.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A list of the skills, knowledge, and abilities a person must have to fill a job.”
why: job specification: A list of the skills, knowledge, and abilities a person must have to fill a job.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An event, typically one or two days, held at a convention center to bring together job seekers and firms that are searching for employees.”
why: job fair: An event, typically one or two days, held at a convention center to bring together job seekers and firms that are searching for employees.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The attempt to find and attract qualified applicants in the external labor market.”
why: recruitment: The attempt to find and attract qualified applicants in the external labor market.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Presenting an accurate and positive image of the firm to those being recruited.”
why: recruitment branding: Presenting an accurate and positive image of the firm to those being recruited.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of determining which persons in the applicant pool possess the qualifications necessary to be successful on the job.”
why: selection: The process of determining which persons in the applicant pool possess the qualifications necessary to be successful on the job.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An in-depth discussion of an applicant’s work experience, skills and abilities, education, and career interests.”
why: selection interview: An in-depth discussion of an applicant’s work experience, skills and abilities, education, and career interests.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A form of on-the-job training that combines specific job instruction with classroom instruction.”
why: apprenticeship: A form of on-the-job training that combines specific job instruction with classroom instruction.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Reassignment of workers to several different jobs over time so that they can learn the basics of each job.”
why: job rotation: Reassignment of workers to several different jobs over time so that they can learn the basics of each job.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A form of on-the-job training in which a senior manager or other experienced employee provides job- and career-related information to a mentee.”
why: mentoring: A form of on-the-job training in which a senior manager or other experienced employee provides job- and career-related information to a mentee.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Presentation to get the new employee ready to perform their job.”
why: orientation: Presentation to get the new employee ready to perform their job.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A form of computer-assisted off-the-job training.”
why: programmed instruction: A form of computer-assisted off-the-job training.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A scaled-down version or mock-up of equipment, processes, or a work environment.”
why: simulation: A scaled-down version or mock-up of equipment, processes, or a work environment.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A comparison of actual performance with expected performance to assess an employee’s contributions to the organization.”
why: performance appraisal: A comparison of actual performance with expected performance to assess an employee’s contributions to the organization.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Additional pay for attaining a specific goal.”
why: incentive pay: Additional pay for attaining a specific goal.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Government payment to unemployed former workers.”
why: unemployment compensation: Government payment to unemployed former workers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Pay for lost work time due to employment-related injuries.”
why: worker’s compensation: Pay for lost work time due to employment-related injuries.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Workers don’t have to join a union but must pay union dues.”
why: agency shop: Workers don’t have to join a union but must pay union dues.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Negotiating a labor agreement.”
why: collective bargaining: Negotiating a labor agreement.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A collection of unions banded together to achieve common goals.”
why: federation: A collection of unions banded together to achieve common goals.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An organization that represents workers in dealing with management.”
why: labor union: An organization that represents workers in dealing with management.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Branch of a national union that represents workers in a specific plant or geographic area.”
why: local union: Branch of a national union that represents workers in a specific plant or geographic area.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Clause in a labor agreement that gives management the right to manage the business except as specified in the contract.”
why: management rights clause: Clause in a labor agreement that gives management the right to manage the business except as specified in the contract.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Settling labor-management disputes through a third party. The decision is final and binding.”
why: arbitration: Settling labor-management disputes through a third party. The decision is final and binding.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A formal complaint by a union worker that management has violated the contract.”
why: grievance: A formal complaint by a union worker that management has violated the contract.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Strike at a critical plant that typically stops operations system-wide.”
why: selective strike strategy: Strike at a critical plant that typically stops operations system-wide.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Programs established by organizations to expand job opportunities for women and minorities.”
why: affirmative action programs: Programs established by organizations to expand job opportunities for women and minorities.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Negotiation process in which a specialist in labor-management negotiations acts as a go-between for management and the unions and helps focus on the problems.”
why: conciliation: Negotiation process in which a specialist in labor-management negotiations acts as a go-between for management and the unions and helps focus on the problems.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Processes discrimination complaints, issues regulations regarding discrimination, and disseminates information.”
why: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC): Processes discrimination complaints, issues regulations regarding discrimination, and disseminates information.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Negotiation process in which a specialist facilitates labor-management contract discussions and suggests compromises.”
why: mediation: Negotiation process in which a specialist facilitates labor-management contract discussions and suggests compromises.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Sets workplace safety and health standards and assures compliance.”
why: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA): Sets workplace safety and health standards and assures compliance.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The specific groups who have legal protection against employment discrimination; include categories of race, national origin, disability, religion, and others.”
why: protected classes: The specific groups who have legal protection against employment discrimination; include categories of race, national origin, disability, religion, and others.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A set of unique features of an organization that are perceived by customers and potential customers as significant and superior to the competition.”
why: competitive advantage: A set of unique features of an organization that are perceived by customers and potential customers as significant and superior to the competition.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Something that prompts a person to release his or her energy in a certain direction.”
why: motivation: Something that prompts a person to release his or her energy in a certain direction.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The gap between what is and what is required.”
why: need: The gap between what is and what is required.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The gap between what is and what is desired.”
why: want: The gap between what is and what is desired.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The phenomenon that employees perform better when they feel singled out for attention or feel that management is concerned about their welfare.”
why: Hawthorne effect: The phenomenon that employees perform better when they feel singled out for attention or feel that management is concerned about their welfare.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Extrinsic elements of the work environment that do not serve as a source of employee satisfaction or motivation.”
why: hygiene factors: Extrinsic elements of the work environment that do not serve as a source of employee satisfaction or motivation.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Intrinsic job elements that lead to worker satisfaction.”
why: motivating factors: Intrinsic job elements that lead to worker satisfaction.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A theory of motivation that holds that worker satisfaction is influenced by employees’ perceptions about how fairly they are treated compared with their coworkers.”
why: equity theory: A theory of motivation that holds that worker satisfaction is influenced by employees’ perceptions about how fairly they are treated compared with their coworkers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A theory of motivation based on the premise that an individual’s intention to work toward a goal is a primary source of motivation.”
why: goal-setting theory: A theory of motivation based on the premise that an individual’s intention to work toward a goal is a primary source of motivation.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Anything that decreases a specific behavior.”
why: punishment: Anything that decreases a specific behavior.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A theory of motivation that holds that people do things because they know that certain consequences will follow.”
why: reinforcement theory: A theory of motivation that holds that people do things because they know that certain consequences will follow.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Anything that increases a specific behavior.”
why: reward: Anything that increases a specific behavior.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The horizontal expansion of a job by increasing the number and variety of tasks that a person performs.”
why: job enlargement: The horizontal expansion of a job by increasing the number and variety of tasks that a person performs.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The vertical expansion of a job by increasing the employee’s autonomy, responsibility, and decision-making authority.”
why: job enrichment: The vertical expansion of a job by increasing the employee’s autonomy, responsibility, and decision-making authority.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The shifting of workers from one job to another; also called cross-training.”
why: job rotation: The shifting of workers from one job to another; also called cross-training.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A scheduling option that allows two individuals to split the tasks, responsibilities, and work hours of one 40-hour-per-week job.”
why: job sharing: A scheduling option that allows two individuals to split the tasks, responsibilities, and work hours of one 40-hour-per-week job.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Management of the production process.”
why: operations management: Management of the production process.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The creation of products and services by turning inputs, such as natural resources, raw materials, human resources, and capital, into outputs, which are products and services.”
why: production: The creation of products and services by turning inputs, such as natural resources, raw materials, human resources, and capital, into outputs, which are products and services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The aspect of operations management in which the firm considers the competitive environment and its own strategic goals in an effort to find the best production methods.”
why: production planning: The aspect of operations management in which the firm considers the competitive environment and its own strategic goals in an effort to find the best production methods.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A production process in which the basic inputs are either combined to create the output or transformed into the output.”
why: assembly process: A production process in which the basic inputs are either combined to create the output or transformed into the output.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A production process that uses long production runs lasting days, weeks, or months without equipment shutdowns; generally used for high-volume, low-variety products with standardized parts.”
why: continuous process: A production process that uses long production runs lasting days, weeks, or months without equipment shutdowns; generally used for high-volume, low-variety products with standardized parts.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The production of goods or services one at a time according to the specific needs or wants of individual customers.”
why: customization: The production of goods or services one at a time according to the specific needs or wants of individual customers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A production process that uses short production runs to make batches of different products; generally used for low-volume, high-variety products.”
why: intermittent process: A production process that uses short production runs to make batches of different products; generally used for low-volume, high-variety products.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A manufacturing firm that produces goods in response to customer orders.”
why: job shop: A manufacturing firm that produces goods in response to customer orders.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A manufacturing process in which goods are mass-produced up to a point and then custom-tailored to the needs or desires of individual customers.”
why: mass customization: A manufacturing process in which goods are mass-produced up to a point and then custom-tailored to the needs or desires of individual customers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Production technique that uses small, self-contained production units, each performing all or most of the tasks necessary to complete a manufacturing order.”
why: cellular manufacturing: Production technique that uses small, self-contained production units, each performing all or most of the tasks necessary to complete a manufacturing order.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A facility arrangement in which the product stays in one place and workers and machinery move to it as needed.”
why: fixed-position layout: A facility arrangement in which the product stays in one place and workers and machinery move to it as needed.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A facility arrangement in which work flows according to the production process. All workers performing similar tasks are grouped together, and products pass from one workstation to another.”
why: process layout: A facility arrangement in which work flows according to the production process. All workers performing similar tasks are grouped together, and products pass from one workstation to another.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A facility arrangement in which workstations or departments are arranged in a line with products moving along the line.”
why: product (or assembly-line) layout: A facility arrangement in which workstations or departments are arranged in a line with products moving along the line.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A list of the items and the number of each required to make a given product.”
why: bill of material: A list of the items and the number of each required to make a given product.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Refers to a decentralized “public ledger” of all transactions that have ever been executed. It is constantly expanding, as “completed” blocks are added to the ledger with each new transaction.”
why: blockchain technology: Refers to a decentralized “public ledger” of all transactions that have ever been executed. It is constantly expanding, as “completed” blocks are added to the ledger with each new transaction.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The electronic exchange of information between two trading partners.”
