q: Which term matches this definition? “A computerized resource-planning system that incorporates information about the firm’s suppliers and customers with its internally generated data.”
why: enterprise resource planning (ERP): A computerized resource-planning system that incorporates information about the firm’s suppliers and customers with its internally generated data.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The supply of goods that a firm holds for use in production or for sale to customers.”
why: inventory: The supply of goods that a firm holds for use in production or for sale to customers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The determination of how much of each type of inventory a firm will keep on hand and the ordering, receiving, storing, and tracking of inventory.”
why: inventory management: The determination of how much of each type of inventory a firm will keep on hand and the ordering, receiving, storing, and tracking of inventory.

q: Which term matches this definition? “In a critical path method network, the longest path through the linked activities.”
why: critical path: In a critical path method network, the longest path through the linked activities.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A scheduling tool that enables a manager to determine the critical path of activities for a project—the activities that will cause the entire project to fall behind schedule if they are not completed on time.”
why: critical path method (CPM): A scheduling tool that enables a manager to determine the critical path of activities for a project—the activities that will cause the entire project to fall behind schedule if they are not completed on time.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Bar graphs plotted on a time line that show the relationship between scheduled and actual production.”
why: Gantt charts: Bar graphs plotted on a time line that show the relationship between scheduled and actual production.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A scheduling tool that is similar to the CPM method but assigns three time estimates for each activity (optimistic, most probable, and pessimistic); allows managers to anticipate delays and potential problems and schedule accordingly.”
why: program evaluation and review technique (PERT): A scheduling tool that is similar to the CPM method but assigns three time estimates for each activity (optimistic, most probable, and pessimistic); allows managers to anticipate delays and potential problems and schedule accordingly.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The aspect of production control that involves setting out the work flow—the sequence of machines and operations through which the product or service progresses from start to finish.”
why: routing: The aspect of production control that involves setting out the work flow—the sequence of machines and operations through which the product or service progresses from start to finish.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The aspect of production control that involves specifying and controlling the time required for each step in the production process.”
why: scheduling: The aspect of production control that involves specifying and controlling the time required for each step in the production process.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A commitment to constantly seek better ways of doing things in order to achieve greater efficiency and improve quality.”
why: continuous improvement: A commitment to constantly seek better ways of doing things in order to achieve greater efficiency and improve quality.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A set of technical standards designed by the International Organization for Standardization to promote clean production processes to protect the environment.”
why: ISO 14000: A set of technical standards designed by the International Organization for Standardization to promote clean production processes to protect the environment.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A system in which materials arrive exactly when they are needed for production, rather than being stored on-site.”
why: just-in-time (JIT): A system in which materials arrive exactly when they are needed for production, rather than being stored on-site.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Streamlining production by eliminating steps in the production process that do not add benefits that customers want.”
why: lean manufacturing: Streamlining production by eliminating steps in the production process that do not add benefits that customers want.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An award given to recognize U.S. companies that offer goods and services of world-class quality; established by Congress and named for a former secretary of commerce.”
why: Malcolm Baldrige National Quality Award: An award given to recognize U.S. companies that offer goods and services of world-class quality; established by Congress and named for a former secretary of commerce.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Goods and services that meet customer expectations by providing reliable performance.”
why: quality: Goods and services that meet customer expectations by providing reliable performance.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The use of computers to design and test new products and modify existing ones.”
why: computer-aided design (CAD): The use of computers to design and test new products and modify existing ones.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The use of computers to develop and control the production process.”
why: computer-aided manufacturing (CAM): The use of computers to develop and control the production process.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The combination of computerized manufacturing processes (such as robots and flexible manufacturing systems) with other computerized systems that control design, inventory, production, and purchasing.”
why: computer-integrated manufacturing (CIM): The combination of computerized manufacturing processes (such as robots and flexible manufacturing systems) with other computerized systems that control design, inventory, production, and purchasing.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A system that combines automated workstations with computer-controlled transportation devices—automatic guided vehicles (AGV)—that move materials between workstations and into and out of the system.”
why: flexible manufacturing system (FMS): A system that combines automated workstations with computer-controlled transportation devices—automatic guided vehicles (AGV)—that move materials between workstations and into and out of the system.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The technology involved in designing, constructing, and operating computer-controlled machines that can perform tasks independently.”
why: robotics: The technology involved in designing, constructing, and operating computer-controlled machines that can perform tasks independently.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A unified system that has the power to integrate and optimize a company’s sprawling functions by automating much of what it does.”
why: business process management (BPM): A unified system that has the power to integrate and optimize a company’s sprawling functions by automating much of what it does.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The customer’s feeling that a product has met or exceeded expectations.”
why: customer satisfaction: The customer’s feeling that a product has met or exceeded expectations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The ratio of benefits to the sacrifice necessary to obtain those benefits, as determined by the customer; reflects the willingness of customers to actually buy a product.”
why: customer value: The ratio of benefits to the sacrifice necessary to obtain those benefits, as determined by the customer; reflects the willingness of customers to actually buy a product.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process in which two parties give something of value to each other to satisfy their respective needs.”
why: exchange: The process in which two parties give something of value to each other to satisfy their respective needs.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of discovering the needs and wants of potential buyers and customers and then providing goods and services that meet or exceed their expectations.”
why: marketing: The process of discovering the needs and wants of potential buyers and customers and then providing goods and services that meet or exceed their expectations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Identifying consumer needs and then producing the goods or services that will satisfy them while making a profit for the organization.”
why: marketing concept: Identifying consumer needs and then producing the goods or services that will satisfy them while making a profit for the organization.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A strategy that focuses on forging long-term partnerships with customers by offering value and providing customer satisfaction.”
why: relationship marketing: A strategy that focuses on forging long-term partnerships with customers by offering value and providing customer satisfaction.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A set of unique features of a company and its products that are perceived by the target market as significant and superior to those of the competition; also called differential advantage.”
why: competitive advantage: A set of unique features of a company and its products that are perceived by the target market as significant and superior to those of the competition; also called differential advantage.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A firm’s ability to produce a product or service at a lower cost than all other competitors in an industry while maintaining satisfactory profit margins.”
why: cost competitive advantage: A firm’s ability to produce a product or service at a lower cost than all other competitors in an industry while maintaining satisfactory profit margins.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A firm’s ability to provide a unique product or service with a set of features that the target market perceives as important and better than the competitor’s.”
why: differential competitive advantage: A firm’s ability to provide a unique product or service with a set of features that the target market perceives as important and better than the competitor’s.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process in which a firm continually collects and evaluates information about its external environment.”
why: environmental scanning: The process in which a firm continually collects and evaluates information about its external environment.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The traditional 4Ps of marketing: product, price, promotion, place (distribution), now with people added as a key marketing component, which together make up the marketing mix.”
why: five Ps: The traditional 4Ps of marketing: product, price, promotion, place (distribution), now with people added as a key marketing component, which together make up the marketing mix.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A firm’s ability to target and effectively serve a single segment of the market, often within a limited geographic area.”
why: niche competitive advantage: A firm’s ability to target and effectively serve a single segment of the market, often within a limited geographic area.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Creating the means by which products flow from the producer to the consumer.”
why: distribution strategy: Creating the means by which products flow from the producer to the consumer.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The blend of product offering, pricing, promotional methods, distribution system, and strategies for utilizing people that creates an offering that brings a specific group of consumers superior value.”
why: marketing mix: The blend of product offering, pricing, promotional methods, distribution system, and strategies for utilizing people that creates an offering that brings a specific group of consumers superior value.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Setting a price based upon the demand for and cost of a good or service.”
why: pricing strategy: Setting a price based upon the demand for and cost of a good or service.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Taking the good or service and selecting a brand name, packaging, colors, a warranty, accessories, and a service program.”
why: product strategy: Taking the good or service and selecting a brand name, packaging, colors, a warranty, accessories, and a service program.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The actions people take in buying and using goods and services.”
why: buyer behavior: The actions people take in buying and using goods and services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The set of values, ideas, attitudes, and other symbols created to shape human behavior.”
why: culture: The set of values, ideas, attitudes, and other symbols created to shape human behavior.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A way of organizing and grouping how an individual reacts to situations.”
why: personality: A way of organizing and grouping how an individual reacts to situations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Formal and informal groups that influence buyer behavior.”
why: reference groups: Formal and informal groups that influence buyer behavior.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The differentiation of markets based on what a product will do rather than on customer characteristics.”
why: benefit segmentation: The differentiation of markets based on what a product will do rather than on customer characteristics.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The differentiation of markets through the use of categories such as age, education, gender, income, and household size.”
why: demographic segmentation: The differentiation of markets through the use of categories such as age, education, gender, income, and household size.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The differentiation of markets by region of the country, city or county size, market density, or climate.”
why: geographic segmentation: The differentiation of markets by region of the country, city or county size, market density, or climate.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of separating, identifying, and evaluating the layers of a market in order to identify a target market.”
why: market segmentation: The process of separating, identifying, and evaluating the layers of a market in order to identify a target market.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of planning, collecting, and analyzing data relevant to a marketing decision.”
why: marketing research: The process of planning, collecting, and analyzing data relevant to a marketing decision.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A marketing research method in which the investigator monitors respondents’ actions without interacting directly with the respondents; for example, by using cash registers with scanners.”
why: observation research: A marketing research method in which the investigator monitors respondents’ actions without interacting directly with the respondents; for example, by using cash registers with scanners.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Large, expensive items with a long life span that are purchased by businesses for use in making other products or providing a service.”
why: capital products: Large, expensive items with a long life span that are purchased by businesses for use in making other products or providing a service.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Relatively inexpensive items that require little shopping effort and are purchased routinely without planning.”
why: convenience products: Relatively inexpensive items that require little shopping effort and are purchased routinely without planning.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Items (purchased by businesses) that are smaller and less expensive than capital products and usually have a life span of less than one year.”
why: expense items: Items (purchased by businesses) that are smaller and less expensive than capital products and usually have a life span of less than one year.

q: Which term matches this definition? “In marketing, a good, service or idea, along with its perceived attributes and benefits, that creates value for the customer.”
why: product: In marketing, a good, service or idea, along with its perceived attributes and benefits, that creates value for the customer.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Items that are bought after considerable planning, including brand-to-brand and store-to-store comparisons of price, suitability, and style.”
why: shopping products: Items that are bought after considerable planning, including brand-to-brand and store-to-store comparisons of price, suitability, and style.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Items for which consumers search long and hard and for which they refuse to accept substitutes.”
why: specialty products: Items for which consumers search long and hard and for which they refuse to accept substitutes.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A method of generating ideas in which group members suggest as many possibilities as they can without criticizing or evaluating any of the suggestions.”
why: brainstorming: A method of generating ideas in which group members suggest as many possibilities as they can without criticizing or evaluating any of the suggestions.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A group of eight to 12 participants led by a moderator in an in-depth discussion on one particular topic or concept.”
why: focus group: A group of eight to 12 participants led by a moderator in an in-depth discussion on one particular topic or concept.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A new flavor, size, or model using an existing brand name in an existing category.”
why: line extension: A new flavor, size, or model using an existing brand name in an existing category.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The person who develops and implements a complete strategy and marketing program for a specific product or brand.”
why: product manager: The person who develops and implements a complete strategy and marketing program for a specific product or brand.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of testing a new product among potential users.”
why: test marketing: The process of testing a new product among potential users.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The pattern of sales and profits over time for a product or product category; consists of an introductory stage, growth stage, maturity, and decline (and death).”
why: product life cycle: The pattern of sales and profits over time for a product or product category; consists of an introductory stage, growth stage, maturity, and decline (and death).

q: Which term matches this definition? “The strategy of grouping two or more related products together and pricing them as a single product.”
why: bundling: The strategy of grouping two or more related products together and pricing them as a single product.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Computer algorithms that allow for prices to change based on demand.”
why: dynamic pricing: Computer algorithms that allow for prices to change based on demand.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The strategy of pricing products below the normal markup or even below cost to attract customers to a store where they would not otherwise shop.”
why: leader pricing: The strategy of pricing products below the normal markup or even below cost to attract customers to a store where they would not otherwise shop.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A product priced below cost as part of a leader-pricing strategy.”
why: loss leader: A product priced below cost as part of a leader-pricing strategy.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The strategy of setting a price at an odd number to connote a bargain and at an even number to suggest quality.”
why: odd-even (psychological) pricing: The strategy of setting a price at an odd number to connote a bargain and at an even number to suggest quality.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The strategy of selling new products at low prices in the hope of achieving a large sales volume.”
why: penetration pricing: The strategy of selling new products at low prices in the hope of achieving a large sales volume.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Large data sets and systems and solutions developed to manage large accumulations of data.”
why: big data: Large data sets and systems and solutions developed to manage large accumulations of data.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Computerized file of customers’ and potential customers’ profiles and purchase patterns.”
why: marketing database: Computerized file of customers’ and potential customers’ profiles and purchase patterns.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Creating a unique marketing mix for every customer.”
why: one-to-one marketing: Creating a unique marketing mix for every customer.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The traditional 4Ps of marketing: product, price, promotion, and place (distribution), now with packaging added as a key marketing component.”
why: 5Ps: The traditional 4Ps of marketing: product, price, promotion, and place (distribution), now with packaging added as a key marketing component.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Sales representatives of manufacturers and wholesalers.”
why: agents: Sales representatives of manufacturers and wholesalers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of breaking large shipments of similar products into smaller, more usable lots.”
why: breaking bulk: The process of breaking large shipments of similar products into smaller, more usable lots.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Go-betweens that bring buyers and sellers together.”
why: brokers: Go-betweens that bring buyers and sellers together.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Efficiently managing the acquisition of raw materials by the factory and the movement of products from the producer to industrial users and consumers.”
why: distribution (logistics): Efficiently managing the acquisition of raw materials by the factory and the movement of products from the producer to industrial users and consumers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The series of marketing entities through which goods and services pass on their way from producers to end users.”
why: distribution channel: The series of marketing entities through which goods and services pass on their way from producers to end users.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A producer; an organization that converts raw materials to finished products.”
why: manufacturer: A producer; an organization that converts raw materials to finished products.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Salespeople who represent noncompeting manufacturers; function as independent agents rather than as salaried employees of the manufacturers.”
why: manufacturers’ representatives: Salespeople who represent noncompeting manufacturers; function as independent agents rather than as salaried employees of the manufacturers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An institution that buys goods from manufacturers (takes ownership) and resells them to businesses, government agencies, other wholesalers, or retailers.”
why: merchant wholesaler: An institution that buys goods from manufacturers (takes ownership) and resells them to businesses, government agencies, other wholesalers, or retailers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Any paid form of nonpersonal presentation by an identified sponsor.”
why: advertising: Any paid form of nonpersonal presentation by an identified sponsor.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The attempt by marketers to inform, persuade, or remind consumers and industrial users to engage in the exchange process.”
why: promotion: The attempt by marketers to inform, persuade, or remind consumers and industrial users to engage in the exchange process.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The combination of advertising, personal selling, sales promotion, and public relations used to promote a product.”
why: promotional mix: The combination of advertising, personal selling, sales promotion, and public relations used to promote a product.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The channels through which advertising is carried to prospective customers; includes print media, broadcast media, outdoor advertising, and online advertising including social media.”
why: advertising media: The channels through which advertising is carried to prospective customers; includes print media, broadcast media, outdoor advertising, and online advertising including social media.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An advertising medium’s ability to reach a precisely defined market.”
why: audience selectivity: An advertising medium’s ability to reach a precisely defined market.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Cost per thousand contacts is a term used in expressing advertising costs; refers to the cost of reaching 1,000 members of the target market.”
why: cost per thousand (CPM): Cost per thousand contacts is a term used in expressing advertising costs; refers to the cost of reaching 1,000 members of the target market.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The number of times an individual is exposed to an advertising message.”
why: frequency: The number of times an individual is exposed to an advertising message.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The number of different target consumers who are exposed to a commercial at least once during a specific period, usually four weeks.”
why: reach: The number of different target consumers who are exposed to a commercial at least once during a specific period, usually four weeks.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A face-to-face sales presentation to a prospective customer.”
why: personal selling: A face-to-face sales presentation to a prospective customer.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of looking for sales prospects.”
why: prospecting: The process of looking for sales prospects.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Inquiries used by salespeople to separate prospects from those who do not have the potential to buy.”
why: qualifying questions: Inquiries used by salespeople to separate prospects from those who do not have the potential to buy.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The companies and people who are most likely to buy a seller’s offerings.”
why: sales prospects: The companies and people who are most likely to buy a seller’s offerings.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Marketing events or sales efforts—not including advertising, personal selling, and public relations—that stimulate buying.”
why: sales promotion: Marketing events or sales efforts—not including advertising, personal selling, and public relations—that stimulate buying.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Any communication or activity designed to win goodwill or prestige for a company or person.”
why: public relations: Any communication or activity designed to win goodwill or prestige for a company or person.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Information about a company or product that appears in the news media and is not directly paid for by the company.”
why: publicity: Information about a company or product that appears in the news media and is not directly paid for by the company.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A marketing channel that includes platforms such as Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram.”
why: social media: A marketing channel that includes platforms such as Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram.

q: Which term matches this definition? “E-commerce refers to the development and maintenance of a company’s website and the facilitation of commerce on the website, such as the ability for customers to order products online and other activities.”
why: e-commerce: E-commerce refers to the development and maintenance of a company’s website and the facilitation of commerce on the website, such as the ability for customers to order products online and other activities.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An executive with responsibility for managing all information resources in an organization.”
why: chief information officer (CIO): An executive with responsibility for managing all information resources in an organization.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An electronic filing system that collects and organizes data and information.”
why: database: An electronic filing system that collects and organizes data and information.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The equipment and techniques used to manage and process information.”
why: information technology (IT): The equipment and techniques used to manage and process information.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A worker who develops or uses knowledge, contributing to and benefiting from information used to perform planning, acquiring, searching, analyzing, organizing, storing, programming, producing, distributing, marketing, or selling functions.”
why: knowledge worker: A worker who develops or uses knowledge, contributing to and benefiting from information used to perform planning, acquiring, searching, analyzing, organizing, storing, programming, producing, distributing, marketing, or selling functions.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The methods and equipment that provide information about all aspects of a firm’s operations.”
why: management information system (MIS): The methods and equipment that provide information about all aspects of a firm’s operations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A service company that buys and maintains software on its servers and distributes it through high-speed networks to subscribers for a set period and price.”
why: application service providers (ASP): A service company that buys and maintains software on its servers and distributes it through high-speed networks to subscribers for a set period and price.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A group of two or more computer systems linked together by communications channels to share data and information.”
why: computer network: A group of two or more computer systems linked together by communications channels to share data and information.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A customizable internal website that provides proprietary corporate information to a defined user group, such as employees, supply-chain partners, or customers.”
why: enterprise portal: A customizable internal website that provides proprietary corporate information to a defined user group, such as employees, supply-chain partners, or customers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An internal corporate-wide area network that uses internet technology to connect computers and link employees in many locations and with different types of computers.”
why: intranet: An internal corporate-wide area network that uses internet technology to connect computers and link employees in many locations and with different types of computers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A network that connects computers at one site, enabling the computer users to exchange data and share the use of hardware and software from a variety of computer manufacturers.”
why: local area network (LAN): A network that connects computers at one site, enabling the computer users to exchange data and share the use of hardware and software from a variety of computer manufacturers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Next generation of ASPs, offering customization and expanded capabilities such as business processes and complete management of the network servers.”
why: managed service providers (MSP): Next generation of ASPs, offering customization and expanded capabilities such as business processes and complete management of the network servers.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A method of updating a database in which data are collected over some time period and processed together.”
why: batch processing: A method of updating a database in which data are collected over some time period and processed together.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Special subset of a data warehouse that deals with a single area of data and is organized for quick analysis.”
why: data mart: Special subset of a data warehouse that deals with a single area of data and is organized for quick analysis.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An information technology that combines many databases across a whole company into one central database that supports management decision-making.”
why: data warehouse: An information technology that combines many databases across a whole company into one central database that supports management decision-making.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A management support system that helps managers make decisions using interactive computer models that describe real-world processes.”
why: decision support system (DSS): A management support system that helps managers make decisions using interactive computer models that describe real-world processes.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A management support system that is customized for an individual executive; provides specific information for strategic decisions.”
why: executive information system (EIS): A management support system that is customized for an individual executive; provides specific information for strategic decisions.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A management support system that gives managers advice similar to what they would get from a human consultant; it uses artificial intelligence to enable computers to reason and learn to solve problems in much the same way humans do.”
why: expert system: A management support system that gives managers advice similar to what they would get from a human consultant; it uses artificial intelligence to enable computers to reason and learn to solve problems in much the same way humans do.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of researching, gathering, organizing, and sharing an organization’s collective knowledge to improve productivity, foster innovation, and gain competitive advantage.”
why: knowledge management (KM): The process of researching, gathering, organizing, and sharing an organization’s collective knowledge to improve productivity, foster innovation, and gain competitive advantage.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A computer program that copies itself into other software and can spread to other computer systems.”
why: computer virus: A computer program that copies itself into other software and can spread to other computer systems.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Sophisticated database applications that look for hidden patterns in a group of data to help track and predict future behavior.”
why: data mining: Sophisticated database applications that look for hidden patterns in a group of data to help track and predict future behavior.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A general term for the delivery of hosted services over the internet.”
why: cloud computing: A general term for the delivery of hosted services over the internet.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of collecting, recording, classifying, summarizing, reporting, and analyzing financial activities.”
why: accounting: The process of collecting, recording, classifying, summarizing, reporting, and analyzing financial activities.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A yearly document that describes a firm’s financial status and usually discusses the firm’s activities during the past year and its prospects for the future.”
why: annual report: A yearly document that describes a firm’s financial status and usually discusses the firm’s activities during the past year and its prospects for the future.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Accounting that focuses on preparing external financial reports that are used by outsiders such as lenders, suppliers, investors, and government agencies to assess the financial strength of a business.”
why: financial accounting: Accounting that focuses on preparing external financial reports that are used by outsiders such as lenders, suppliers, investors, and government agencies to assess the financial strength of a business.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The private organization that is responsible for establishing financial accounting standards in the United States.”
why: Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB): The private organization that is responsible for establishing financial accounting standards in the United States.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The financial accounting standards followed by accountants in the United States when preparing financial statements.”
why: generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP): The financial accounting standards followed by accountants in the United States when preparing financial statements.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Accounting that provides financial information that managers inside the organization can use to evaluate and make decisions about current and future operations.”
why: managerial accounting: Accounting that provides financial information that managers inside the organization can use to evaluate and make decisions about current and future operations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of reviewing the records used to prepare financial statements and issuing a formal auditor’s opinion indicating whether the statements have been prepared in accordance with accepted accounting rules.”
why: auditing: The process of reviewing the records used to prepare financial statements and issuing a formal auditor’s opinion indicating whether the statements have been prepared in accordance with accepted accounting rules.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A managerial accountant who has completed a professional certification program, including passing an examination.”
why: certified management accountant (CMA): A managerial accountant who has completed a professional certification program, including passing an examination.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An accountant who has completed an approved bachelor’s degree program, passed a test prepared by the American Institute of CPAs, and met state requirements. Only a CPA can issue an auditor’s opinion on a firm’s financial statements.”
why: certified public accountant (CPA): An accountant who has completed an approved bachelor’s degree program, passed a test prepared by the American Institute of CPAs, and met state requirements. Only a CPA can issue an auditor’s opinion on a firm’s financial statements.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Accountants who are employed to serve one particular organization.”
why: private accountants: Accountants who are employed to serve one particular organization.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Independent accountants who serve organizations and individuals on a fee basis.”
why: public accountants: Independent accountants who serve organizations and individuals on a fee basis.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Things of value owned by a firm.”
why: assets: Things of value owned by a firm.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A method of accounting in which each transaction is recorded as two entries so that two accounts or records are changed.”
why: double-entry bookkeeping: A method of accounting in which each transaction is recorded as two entries so that two accounts or records are changed.

q: Which term matches this definition? “What a firm owes to its creditors; also called debts.”
why: liabilities: What a firm owes to its creditors; also called debts.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The total amount of investment in the firm minus any liabilities; also called net worth.”
why: owners’ equity: The total amount of investment in the firm minus any liabilities; also called net worth.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A financial statement that summarizes a firm’s financial position at a specific point in time.”
why: balance sheet: A financial statement that summarizes a firm’s financial position at a specific point in time.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Assets that can or will be converted to cash within the next 12 months.”
why: current assets: Assets that can or will be converted to cash within the next 12 months.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Short-term claims that are due within a year of the date of the balance sheet.”
why: current liabilities: Short-term claims that are due within a year of the date of the balance sheet.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The allocation of an asset’s original cost to the years in which it is expected to produce revenues.”
why: depreciation: The allocation of an asset’s original cost to the years in which it is expected to produce revenues.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Long-term assets used by a firm for more than a year such as land, buildings, and machinery.”
why: fixed assets: Long-term assets used by a firm for more than a year such as land, buildings, and machinery.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Long-term assets with no physical existence, such as patents, copyrights, trademarks, and goodwill.”
why: intangible assets: Long-term assets with no physical existence, such as patents, copyrights, trademarks, and goodwill.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The total expense of buying or producing a firm’s goods or services.”
why: cost of goods sold: The total expense of buying or producing a firm’s goods or services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The costs of generating revenues.”
why: expenses: The costs of generating revenues.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The amount a company earns after paying to produce or buy its products but before deducting operating expenses.”
why: gross profit: The amount a company earns after paying to produce or buy its products but before deducting operating expenses.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The total dollar amount of a company’s sales.”
why: gross sales: The total dollar amount of a company’s sales.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A financial statement that summarizes a firm’s revenues and expenses and shows its total profit or loss over a period of time.”
why: income statement: A financial statement that summarizes a firm’s revenues and expenses and shows its total profit or loss over a period of time.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The amount obtained by subtracting all of a firm’s expenses from its revenues, when the expenses are more than the revenues.”
why: net loss: The amount obtained by subtracting all of a firm’s expenses from its revenues, when the expenses are more than the revenues.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A financial statement that provides a summary of the money flowing into and out of a firm during a certain period, typically one year.”
why: statement of cash flows: A financial statement that provides a summary of the money flowing into and out of a firm during a certain period, typically one year.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The ratio of total current assets excluding inventory to total current liabilities; used to measure a firm’s liquidity.”
why: acid-test (quick) ratio: The ratio of total current assets excluding inventory to total current liabilities; used to measure a firm’s liquidity.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Ratios that measure how well a firm uses its assets.”
why: activity ratios: Ratios that measure how well a firm uses its assets.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The ratio of total current assets to total current liabilities; used to measure a firm’s liquidity.”
why: current ratio: The ratio of total current assets to total current liabilities; used to measure a firm’s liquidity.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Ratios that measure the degree and effect of a firm’s use of borrowed funds (debt) to finance its operations.”
why: debt ratios: Ratios that measure the degree and effect of a firm’s use of borrowed funds (debt) to finance its operations.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The ratio of total liabilities to owners’ equity; measures the relationship between the amount of debt financing (borrowing) and the amount of equity financing (owner’s funds).”
why: debt-to-equity ratio: The ratio of total liabilities to owners’ equity; measures the relationship between the amount of debt financing (borrowing) and the amount of equity financing (owner’s funds).

q: Which term matches this definition? “The ratio of net profit to the number of shares of common stock outstanding; measures the number of dollars earned by each share of stock.”
why: earnings per share (EPS): The ratio of net profit to the number of shares of common stock outstanding; measures the number of dollars earned by each share of stock.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Cash held in the form of coins and paper money.”
why: currency: Cash held in the form of coins and paper money.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Money kept in accounts that can be withdrawn by depositors on demand.”
why: demand deposits: Money kept in accounts that can be withdrawn by depositors on demand.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The total amount of readily available money in the system; includes currency and demand deposits.”
why: M1: The total amount of readily available money in the system; includes currency and demand deposits.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A term used by economists to describe the U.S. monetary supply. Includes all M1 monies plus time deposits and other money that is not immediately accessible.”
why: M2: A term used by economists to describe the U.S. monetary supply. Includes all M1 monies plus time deposits and other money that is not immediately accessible.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Anything that is acceptable as payment for goods and services.”
why: money: Anything that is acceptable as payment for goods and services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Deposits at a bank or other financial institution that pay interest but cannot be withdrawn on demand.”
why: time deposits: Deposits at a bank or other financial institution that pay interest but cannot be withdrawn on demand.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The interest rate that the Federal Reserve charges its member banks.”
why: discount rate: The interest rate that the Federal Reserve charges its member banks.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The central bank of the United States; consists of 12 district banks, each located in a major U.S. city.”
why: Federal Reserve System (Fed): The central bank of the United States; consists of 12 district banks, each located in a major U.S. city.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The purchase or sale of U.S. government bonds by the Federal Reserve to stimulate or slow down the economy.”
why: open market operations: The purchase or sale of U.S. government bonds by the Federal Reserve to stimulate or slow down the economy.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Requires banks that are members of the Federal Reserve System to hold some of their deposits in cash in their vaults or in an account at a district bank.”
why: reserve requirement: Requires banks that are members of the Federal Reserve System to hold some of their deposits in cash in their vaults or in an account at a district bank.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The power of the Federal Reserve to control consumer credit rules and margin requirements.”
why: selective credit controls: The power of the Federal Reserve to control consumer credit rules and margin requirements.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An operating license issued to a bank by the federal government or a state government; required for a commercial bank to do business.”
why: bank charter: An operating license issued to a bank by the federal government or a state government; required for a commercial bank to do business.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Profit-oriented financial institutions that accept deposits, make business and consumer loans, invest in government and corporate securities, and provide other financial services.”
why: commercial banks: Profit-oriented financial institutions that accept deposits, make business and consumer loans, invest in government and corporate securities, and provide other financial services.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Not-for-profit, member-owned financial cooperatives.”
why: credit unions: Not-for-profit, member-owned financial cooperatives.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process in which financial institutions act as intermediaries between the suppliers and demanders of funds.”
why: financial intermediation: The process in which financial institutions act as intermediaries between the suppliers and demanders of funds.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Large pools of money set aside by corporations, unions, and governments for later use in paying retirement benefits to their employees or members.”
why: pension funds: Large pools of money set aside by corporations, unions, and governments for later use in paying retirement benefits to their employees or members.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Depository institutions formed specifically to encourage household saving and to make home mortgage loans.”
why: thrift institutions: Depository institutions formed specifically to encourage household saving and to make home mortgage loans.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An independent, quasi-public corporation backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government that insures deposits in commercial banks and thrift institutions for up to a ceiling of $250,000 per account.”
why: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC): An independent, quasi-public corporation backed by the full faith and credit of the U.S. government that insures deposits in commercial banks and thrift institutions for up to a ceiling of $250,000 per account.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The inflow and outflow of cash for a firm.”
why: cash flows: The inflow and outflow of cash for a firm.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The art and science of managing a firm’s money so that it can meet its goals.”
why: financial management: The art and science of managing a firm’s money so that it can meet its goals.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The opportunity for profit.”
why: return: The opportunity for profit.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The potential for loss or the chance that an investment will not achieve the expected level of return.”
why: risk: The potential for loss or the chance that an investment will not achieve the expected level of return.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A basic principle in finance that holds that the higher the risk, the greater the return that is required.”
why: risk-return trade-off: A basic principle in finance that holds that the higher the risk, the greater the return that is required.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Sales for which a firm has not yet been paid.”
why: accounts receivable: Sales for which a firm has not yet been paid.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of analyzing long-term projects and selecting those that offer the best returns while maximizing the firm’s value.”
why: capital budgeting: The process of analyzing long-term projects and selecting those that offer the best returns while maximizing the firm’s value.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Investments in long-lived assets, such as land, buildings, machinery, equipment, and information services, that are expected to provide benefits over a period longer than one year.”
why: capital expenditures: Investments in long-lived assets, such as land, buildings, machinery, equipment, and information services, that are expected to provide benefits over a period longer than one year.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The process of making sure that a firm has enough cash on hand to pay bills as they come due and to meet unexpected expenses.”
why: cash management: The process of making sure that a firm has enough cash on hand to pay bills as they come due and to meet unexpected expenses.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Unsecured short-term debt—an IOU—issued by a financially strong corporation.”
why: commercial paper: Unsecured short-term debt—an IOU—issued by a financially strong corporation.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Short-term investments that are easily converted into cash.”
why: marketable securities: Short-term investments that are easily converted into cash.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Purchases for which a buyer has not yet paid the seller.”
why: accounts payable: Purchases for which a buyer has not yet paid the seller.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A form of short-term financing in which a firm sells its accounts receivable outright at a discount to a factor.”
why: factoring: A form of short-term financing in which a firm sells its accounts receivable outright at a discount to a factor.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An agreement between a bank and a business that specifies the maximum amount of unsecured short-term borrowing the bank will allow the firm over a given period, typically one year.”
why: line of credit: An agreement between a bank and a business that specifies the maximum amount of unsecured short-term borrowing the bank will allow the firm over a given period, typically one year.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A guaranteed line of credit whereby a bank agrees that a certain amount of funds will be available for a business to borrow over a given period, typically two to five years.”
why: revolving credit agreement: A guaranteed line of credit whereby a bank agrees that a certain amount of funds will be available for a business to borrow over a given period, typically two to five years.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Loans for which the borrower is required to pledge specific assets as collateral, or security.”
why: secured loans: Loans for which the borrower is required to pledge specific assets as collateral, or security.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The extension of credit by the seller to the buyer between the time the buyer receives the goods or services and when it pays for them.”
why: trade credit: The extension of credit by the seller to the buyer between the time the buyer receives the goods or services and when it pays for them.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Long-term debt obligations (liabilities) issued by corporations and governments.”
why: bonds: Long-term debt obligations (liabilities) issued by corporations and governments.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The chance that a firm will be unable to make scheduled interest and principal payments on its debt.”
why: financial risk: The chance that a firm will be unable to make scheduled interest and principal payments on its debt.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A fixed amount of money paid by the issuer of a bond to the bondholder on a regular schedule, typically every six months; stated as the coupon rate.”
why: interest: A fixed amount of money paid by the issuer of a bond to the bondholder on a regular schedule, typically every six months; stated as the coupon rate.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A long-term loan made against real estate as collateral.”
why: mortgage loan: A long-term loan made against real estate as collateral.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The amount borrowed by the issuer of a bond; also called par value.”
why: principal: The amount borrowed by the issuer of a bond; also called par value.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A business loan with a maturity of more than one year; can be unsecured or secured.”
why: term loan: A business loan with a maturity of more than one year; can be unsecured or secured.

q: Which term matches this definition? “A security that represents an ownership interest in a corporation.”
why: common stock: A security that represents an ownership interest in a corporation.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Payments to stockholders from a corporation’s profits.”
why: dividends: Payments to stockholders from a corporation’s profits.

q: Which term matches this definition? “An equity security for which the dividend amount is set at the time the stock is issued and the dividend must be paid before the company can pay dividends to common stockholders.”
why: preferred stock: An equity security for which the dividend amount is set at the time the stock is issued and the dividend must be paid before the company can pay dividends to common stockholders.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Profits that have been reinvested in a firm.”
why: retained earnings: Profits that have been reinvested in a firm.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Payments to stockholders in the form of more stock; may replace or supplement cash dividends.”
why: stock dividends: Payments to stockholders in the form of more stock; may replace or supplement cash dividends.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Letter grades assigned to bond issues to indicate their quality or level of risk; assigned by rating agencies such as Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s (S&P).”
why: bond ratings: Letter grades assigned to bond issues to indicate their quality or level of risk; assigned by rating agencies such as Moody’s and Standard & Poor’s (S&P).

q: Which term matches this definition? “A security similar to a mutual fund; holds a broad basket of stocks with a common theme but trades on a stock exchange so that its price changes throughout the day.”
why: exchange traded fund (ETF): A security similar to a mutual fund; holds a broad basket of stocks with a common theme but trades on a stock exchange so that its price changes throughout the day.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Legally binding obligations to buy or sell specified quantities of commodities or financial instruments at an agreed-on price at a future date.”
why: futures contracts: Legally binding obligations to buy or sell specified quantities of commodities or financial instruments at an agreed-on price at a future date.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Investment professionals who are paid to manage other people’s money.”
why: institutional investors: Investment professionals who are paid to manage other people’s money.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Firms that act as intermediaries, buying securities from corporations and governments and reselling them to the public.”
why: investment bankers: Firms that act as intermediaries, buying securities from corporations and governments and reselling them to the public.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Bonds issued by states, cities, counties, and other state and local government agencies.”
why: municipal bonds: Bonds issued by states, cities, counties, and other state and local government agencies.

q: Which term matches this definition? “National and regional securities exchanges that bring buyers and sellers together through brokers on a centralized trading floor.”
why: broker markets: National and regional securities exchanges that bring buyers and sellers together through brokers on a centralized trading floor.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Corrective measures that, under certain conditions, stop trading in the securities markets for a short cooling-off period to limit the amount the market can drop in one day.”
why: circuit breakers: Corrective measures that, under certain conditions, stop trading in the securities markets for a short cooling-off period to limit the amount the market can drop in one day.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Securities markets where buy and sell orders are executed through dealers, or “market makers,” linked by telecommunications networks.”
why: dealer markets: Securities markets where buy and sell orders are executed through dealers, or “market makers,” linked by telecommunications networks.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Private trading networks that allow institutional traders and some individuals to make direct transactions in the fourth market.”
why: electronic communications networks (ECNs): Private trading networks that allow institutional traders and some individuals to make direct transactions in the fourth market.

q: Which term matches this definition? “The use of information that is not available to the general public to make profits on securities transactions.”
why: insider trading: The use of information that is not available to the general public to make profits on securities transactions.

q: Which term matches this definition? “Markets, other than the exchanges, on which small companies trade; includes the Over-the-Counter Bulletin Board (OTCBB) and the Pink Sheets.”
why: over-the-counter (OTC) market: Markets, other than the exchanges, on which small companies trade; includes the Over-the-Counter Bulletin Board (OTCBB) and the Pink Sheets.
